title: Opera's WebAI runs a local model in the browser, if you opt in
friendlyTitle: Opera is letting a web page use a model on your computer, if you opt in
summary: Opera has opened an early preview of WebAI in Opera One. It is Opera's proposal for letting a page use a model on the device, rather than a cloud API. Opera says it is not tied to one model, names Google's Gemma as an example, and says Macs can use Apple's on-device foundation model. Opera GX and Opera Neon are due to follow. The feature is opt-in.
friendlySummary: Opera has opened an early preview of WebAI in its Opera One browser. It is Opera's proposal for letting a web page use a model on the device, instead of sending the job to a cloud service. Opera says it is not locked to one model. It names Google's Gemma as an example, and says Macs can use Apple's on-device model. Opera GX and Opera Neon are due to get the same feature. You have to turn it on.
whyItMatters: The practical offer is a page that can generate or classify text without a per-request bill, with the prompt staying on the machine. Opera also says speed depends on the hardware. This is Opera's preview, not a standard other browsers have adopted. The useful test is whether a site you already use can do a small job without a subscription.
